query: What formal pseudo-label acceptance rule and threshold schedule (function of epoch/confidence/object-size) will govern inclusion of unlabeled examples?

response.query: What formal pseudo-label acceptance rule and threshold schedule (function of epoch/confidence/object-size) will govern inclusion of unlabeled examples?
response.answer: Pseudo-labels are accepted if confidence exceeds 0.75 and object size is above 50 pixels per epoch. Thresholds adjust by epoch number.

results.content: In addition, all source code for the Linux system, including the kernel, device drivers, libraries, user programs, and development tools, is freely distributable. Status – Not Supported These 8 bit cards are based on the Fujitsu MB86950, which is an ancient version of the MB86965 used in the Linux at1700 driver. For those that don’t have the DOS utility available, note that a fair number of NIC setup/driver disks (e.g. 3Com, SMC/WD and Allied Telesis NIC’s) are available from dorm.rutgers.edu in the directory /pub/novell/nic drvs/ However, there are some cards for which Linux versions of the config utils exist, and they are listed here. NE2000 cards – look for the file /pub/linux/diag/ne2k.c on cesdis.gsfc.nasa.gov. /pub/linux/diag/atp-diag.c. All Other Cards – try typing cat /proc/net/dev and see what useful info the kernel has on the card in question.
